pr_title: Teach EdDSA signature algorithms about AlgorithmIdentifiers
pr_body:
The other signature algorithms know how to create their own
AlgorithmIdentifiers, but the EdDSA algorithms missed this.

Fixes #11875
pr_comments:
> Need to update EVP_SIGNATURE-ED25519.pod. (See EVP_SIGNATURE-ECDSA.pod)

Documentation added. Also a fixup pushed to address the travis failure.
This pull request is ready to merge

issue_context.title: OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha2 EdDSA X509 signing
issue_context.body:
In OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha2 ed25519 and ed448 keys fail when trying to use them to sign with `X509_sign`, `X509_CRL_sign`, and `X509_REQ_sign`. Based on some of the conversation in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/11845 this could also possibly be an instance of a function not understanding provider side keys yet, but that is pure speculation on my part.

No errors are added to the stack, but the functions return 0.

Calling `EVP_PKEY_id` on ed25519/ed448 public keys returned from `X509_get_pubkey` also returns a 0 when we expect `NID_ED25519` (or the equivalent for ed448)
comments: Just a nudge to say this is still an issue on the latest master.
Do you have any reproducer code?
Thanks for the reproducer - that was very helpful. Fix in #12884.
Thanks @mattcaswell. I pulled that PR, built the library, and then build `pyca/cryptography` against it to run our test suite. All X509 tests now pass.

review_comments:
FWIW I would be very surprised if parameters were defined in the future.
A major design point/goal was to have these be simple, with no parameters, with inputs/outputs as fixed-length byte strings.
